profile.campus: Gallatin, Sumner County, Tennessee (Meta's Gallatin data center campus)
profile.address: Roundtree Drive, Sumner County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee, 37066
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 1 of 3 mapped in the newer cluster, westernmost to easternmost ordering) is part of Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee, northeast of Nashville. Facebook announced the project in August 2020 after a three-year site-selection effort involving the Gallatin Economic Development Agency, the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development, and the Tennessee Valley Authority; the initial building was reported at 982,000 square feet with an $800 million investment, citing the area's infrastructure, workforce, and community partnership. Meta's own announcement confirms the Gallatin data center went live on November 14, 2024, with total Tennessee investment since grown to more than $1.5 billion, more than 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and now more than 100 operational jobs. TVA initially committed to bringing 220 megawatts of new solar generation to support the project; Meta's current fact sheet describes a Meta-supported total of 530 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity added in Tennessee as the campus has grown, alongside the facility's standard commitments to 100% renewable electricity, LEED Gold certification, and roughly 80% less water use than an average data center. Meta reports more than $1.4 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, including a $250,000 grant to the Gallatin Shalom Zone for restoration of a historic gymnasium, 30 acres of native pollinator habitat planted on-site, and a partnership with the Tennessee Environmental Council to install roughly 6,000 square feet of pollinator gardens across Sumner County middle schools. Meta does not publish a specific street address, current building count, or per-building square footage for individual Gallatin structures beyond the original 982,000-square-foot building reported at announcement; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

sources.title: Facebook to Build $800 Million Data Center in Gallatin, Tennessee

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity or MW for Gallatin; the original building was reported at 982,000 square feet at its 2020 announcement, and the campus has since grown with TVA-linked renewable energy commitments reaching a Meta-supported 530 megawatts statewide. No confirmed current building count or additional per-building square footage is asserted here.
profile.facility_note: One of three Meta buildings OpenStreetMap groups together at this Gallatin location.

profile.regional_context: Sumner County sits in the Nashville metro area and has drawn additional large-scale investment alongside Meta's data center; Gallatin's selection followed a multi-year TVA- and state-backed economic-development recruitment process typical of Middle Tennessee's growing data-center and advanced-manufacturing corridor.

reading.body:
Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County is a hyperscale facility with no published power capacity, making it impossible to estimate its compute footprint or rank it among Tennessee data centers by IT load. Meta invested $1.5B+ starting from a 2020 groundbreaking and operates it for 70+ staff, but the absence of published megawatts means this site cannot be assessed against the four Tennessee facilities that have disclosed power figures totaling 12.13 MW.

The campus achieves LEED Gold certification for operational buildings and procures 100 percent renewable energy matching its electricity use as part of Meta's net-zero operations. A Meta-supported renewable project is adding 530 MW of generation capacity in Tennessee, though the split between this campus and other state users is not published. Without the campus's own power draw, it is not possible to determine how much of that renewable deployment serves this facility versus other Meta infrastructure or state grid demands.

Gallatin is one of 24 mapped data center facilities in Tennessee, but one of only four with published capacity figures from operator spec pages. The refusal to disclose power consumption is standard practice at major cloud operators and makes capacity assessment dependent on future disclosures or indirect methods. Until Meta publishes the Gallatin campus's megawatt draw, this site cannot determine whether the facility is significant to AI scaling constraints in Tennessee or across the US grid.
